# Splenic vein thrombosis

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Cardiology and angiology > Vascular diseases > Splenic vein thrombosis*

[Original Article Link](/library/K90UoR)

---

## Summary

<u>Splenic vein</u> <u>thrombosis</u> is most commonly caused by <u>chronic inflammation</u> from adjacent <u>pancreatitis</u>. Other causes include <u>hypercoagulable states</u> and external compression of the <u>splenic vein</u>. Patients are usually asymptomatic but may present with abdominal <u>pain</u>, <u>upper gastrointestinal bleeding</u> (<u>UGIB</u>) from <u>gastric varices</u>, and <u>splenomegaly</u>. Diagnosis is typically confirmed with CT or <u>MRI</u> <u>angiography</u>. Management focuses on treating the underlying cause and using anticoagulation to prevent <u>thrombus</u> growth. For patients with active <u>variceal bleeding</u>, <u>splenectomy</u> is the recommended definitive treatment.

## Epidemiology

* Isolated <u>splenic vein</u> <u>thrombosis</u> (i.e., without concurrent <u>portal vein thrombosis</u>) occurs in approximately:

* 12.4% of patients with <u>chronic pancreatitis</u> [[1]](/library/aYVQnG0)

* 22.6% of patients with <u>acute pancreatitis</u> [[1]](/library/aYVQnG0)



Epidemiological data refers to the US, unless otherwise specified.

---

## Clinical features

* Most patients are asymptomatic. [[1]](/library/aYVQnG0)[[2]](/library/oZV0cG0)

* If symptomatic, manifestations may include: [[2]](/library/oZV0cG0)

* Abdominal <u>pain</u>

* Overt <u>upper GI bleeding</u> from <u>gastric varices</u>

* <u>Splenomegaly</u> in ∼ 70% of patients [[2]](/library/oZV0cG0)
